account:
It is day 1 at six in the morning. I have just woken at home, so I have not yet observed today's town activity. Yesterday's unusual matter was a vague rumor about changes to the bridge or port. I have no evidence that such changes are actually planned, nor do I know what purpose they would serve. Our riverside neighbour had heard the rumor but saw nothing unusual and did not identify a source. The secretary traced a separate report through Townsfolk 03 to the innkeeper, who denied proposing or announcing changes. I have asked the secretary to arrange a conversation with Townsfolk 03 today without displacing my appointments, to learn precisely what they heard and from whom.

The practical reports so far suggest ordinary business rather than an emergency. The builder reported the bridge passable with no confirmed defects and relayed Freight's report of undamaged roads and an uneventful morning ferry crossing. Our neighbour said Freight described quiet docks and offered ferry rides and deliveries. The baker reportedly said there was no special celebration planned, only fresh bread for market. These are reports, not my own inspections. The secretary's accounts record contained no claims or receipts, and no repair contract or spending was authorized. Any specific maintenance proposal requires a written estimate and approval.

I remain curious whether the rumor conceals a real proposal, a misunderstanding, or mere gossip. I have not established a secret undertaking or anyone's hidden motive. The secretary has been helping verify information and preserve records. My next priority is to go to the office and read the appointment book, which the secretary retained and promised to have ready for my morning review.
